# Synthetic booth specification

The fictional exhibit occupies a 6,000 mm by 3,000 mm island plot, with the long edge facing the main aisle.

The maximum construction height is 3,200 mm. No suspended element or rigging point is included.

The north wall is 2,700 mm high and uses matte white reusable panels.

The east return wall is 1,800 mm wide, leaving a 1,200 mm clear opening beside it.

The primary aisle must remain clear for 1,500 mm from the plot boundary.

An accessible route at least 1,200 mm wide connects reception to the demonstration zone.

Reception uses one 1,200 by 600 mm counter with a lockable shelf.

The counter top is 900 mm above the finished floor and has rounded front corners.

The decided reception location is the northwest corner, angled toward arriving visitors.

Four stools are prohibited at reception; staff will stand behind the counter.

The central product plinth measures 1,400 by 800 mm and is 750 mm high.

The plinth design load is 180 kg, distributed evenly over its top surface.

A transparent guard rises 250 mm above the plinth around the synthetic mechanism.

The demonstration zone requires two grounded 100 V outlets rated at 15 A each.

Power cables run beneath approved cable covers and never cross the accessible route uncovered.

One 55-inch display is fixed to the north wall with its center at 1,550 mm.

The display input is HDMI, and a spare three-meter cable is stored on site.

Audio playback is disabled by decision; captions are embedded in every demonstration video.

The main sign is 2,800 mm wide by 500 mm high and begins at elevation 2,400 mm.

Sign lettering uses fictional brand name Northstar Example in dark blue on white.

No real company names, product marks, client names, or event identifiers appear in graphics.

Six track lights use neutral 4,000 K lamps with individual aiming adjustment.

Lighting circuits are separated from the demonstration equipment circuit.

The meeting area contains one 900 mm round table and four stackable chairs.

Chair backs stay within the plot line even when occupied.

A 1,500 by 1,200 mm store room sits in the southeast corner.

The store door opens inward and provides a clear opening of 800 mm.

The store contains one shelf rated for 30 kg per level and a coat rail.

All exposed floor uses charcoal carpet tile with taped, flush perimeter edges.

The product zone receives a removable pale-gray vinyl insert measuring 2,000 by 1,500 mm.

No platform or raised floor is approved; every transition remains level.

The fire extinguisher and venue alarm point remain visible and unobstructed.

Materials carry the fictional venue's required flame-retardant documentation.

Installation begins at 09:00 on the day before opening and finishes by 17:00.

The electrical inspection is scheduled after wall completion and before product placement.

Two installers verify every wall brace and record the check on an anonymous sheet.

The decided visitor flow enters from northwest, circles the plinth clockwise, and exits southwest.

Emergency egress may reverse that flow without passing through the meeting furniture.

Waste is separated into board, metal, plastics, and general refuse during dismantling.

Dismantling begins only after the fictional organizer announces hall closure.

The final handover includes dimension checks, surface photographs, and a signed synthetic checklist.

Any on-site dimensional conflict is escalated before cutting material or relocating equipment.
